title: I built something While building trading Bots for 7 Months and just realized it last week
author: Moedawi85
selftext: So I've been working on 3 bots for the last 7 months, some days they do good with paper trading but most of the time just straight trash (I don't know much about trading and my knowledge is just the same as ur average guy). I also built an app to control and monitor the bots and decided to add my IRA account after transferring it to Alpaca IRA. The way these but work i give it a specific rules of what to look for which is basically ETFs and Thin Cap and decided to trade on my IRA manually through the app plus having more than 10 custome exits that no other trading app has, what I've been doing in the morning at 9:31 basically waiting on the apps pilot to flag tickers that just has volume spike 3 times it's average and drop 100 dollars in each flag, within 5 min if I dont get 5% I drop the ticker and keep the moving ones, and twice I ended up landing on really good tickers. The 1st one was on the 23rd put 5k into a ticker it went up to 1500 in profit and it got halted, while I'm showing my coworker I got halted at 1500 it went up to 5K so I sold immediately and made 5k. Now Friday I risked it all for the big biscuit, I was doing my shuffle and down 1300 and I found one of the tickers I bought is moving quick, quickly I added more money totaling 15K and it went up to 17% so I set my tightest exit at worst id be giving back 5K, and I said to myself when the halted is done I'm either gonna ride the continues peak or the adjust price would be below my floor but i should be able to pocket some profit, and that ticker was MSGY, it halted for 30 MIn so instead of waiting on I wanted to switch out my desk layout in the office I put the phone down and started working, 20 min later I look at my phone and it sold so I look the selling price and I'm like hmm 1500 not bad but i looked again an it's 15k I made 102%. So not only I made money every single day last week but 2 days I made a total of 20K. I realized it wasn't the bots that I should've paid attention to this whole time by the app structural, the exit laws, and mainly the scanner feed.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the honest bit in this post is that the bots were trash on paper for seven months and the thing that made money was you, at 9:31, with a five minute rule and a halt. that rule has run twice. before the next 15k goes in, run it on paper every morning for a month and count what it does, because two good halts in a row is exactly what a coin flip does too.

replies.author: Moedawi85
replies.body: That's actually a good idea, the app has a ledger in it I could try logging the next halted as paper trade.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: logging every halt in that ledger is the whole test. write the entry rule down first (what makes a halt a buy at 9:31, what makes you skip one), then log every one that qualifies, including the ones you'd have chickened out of. a month of that and you'll know if the two wins were the rule or the week.

replies.author: Moedawi85
replies.body: Will Def log them, but usually if i bought something and I'm up over 10% and it halts I'm not worried I could be wrong but I don't think a price adjustment after a halt would be that low. At 5% i def be worried.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: halts that reopen down 30 or 40 percent happen, the news ones especially, so a 10 percent cushion is not a floor. that is exactly what the ledger will show you after a month, which is why I'd log the reopen gap on every halt, not only the ones you were in.

comments.author: AdQueasy4855
comments.body:
It's fine to let AI help you analyze stocks, but I believe it's inadvisable to let AI make your trading decisions. You might do well initially, but you'll inevitably fail later.The logic is simple: there are always more losers than winners in the stock market. If everyone used AI to trade, the stock market couldn't function.

This is just my personal opinion.

comments.author: powerbone
comments.body:
​"Not at all. This screenshot shows clear red flags of a manipulated or fake trading bot scam:
​Unrealistic Curve: The equity jumps vertically in a single step and holds flat, which looks like hardcoded UI data rather than real trading activity.
​Mismatched Numbers: The top percentage (+90.20%) doesn't mathematically align with the total equity ($29,681.47) or the invested amount ($3,997).
​Classic Scam Hook: Phrases like "built this for 7 months and just realized" are standard engagement bait used on Reddit/X to sell fake bots, courses, or referral links."

comments.author: TelephoneHot1933
comments.body: im not sure the bot is even the part worth chasing here. The scanner plus your exit rules sound like where the value came from, but two monster hits can mess with your head fast. I would log every alert the same way for a few weeks and see what the bad ones look like too. If Moon is in the mix I would keep that separate from this test so you can tell what edge is coming from the scanner and what is coming from the trade itself.
